precedence_rule: Newest explicit user approval wins when decisions conflict. A technical build is not treated as a user approval unless the user accepted it or it is part of the accepted lineage without later rejection. Latest user corrections override earlier implementation details.

entries.decision: New device or cleared local state falls back to Today.

New accounts use five-step onboarding: name, recovery date, recovery pathway, belief preference separately, optional city/state; completion lands on Today.
Completed onboarding must not restart on refresh.
Settings -> Review Setup may intentionally reopen onboarding.
An existing Recovery user must not restart the interview merely by clicking Continue Recovery.
entries.basis: Latest explicit user complaint and efficiency correction.

entries.decision: Recovery onboarding/introduction must not be a gate to safety/support.

entries.basis: Observed race: first click restarted interview, second succeeded.

entries.decision: Obsolete blank-box modal must not reappear.
Recovery uses six phases through roughly the first six months: Stabilize, Build, Understand, Rebuild, Strengthen, Grow.
Months 7–12 are Maintenance; Year 1 milestone remains part of the journey.
Year 2 remains supported; Year 3+ becomes a lighter long-term/weekly recovery experience while history and milestones continue.
Current phase is emphasized; future phases remain de-emphasized/hidden until appropriate.
entries.basis: Approved progressive disclosure and RC QA.

entries.decision: Prior content/history remains intentionally accessible.
Today includes guided Check-In, Daily Focus, Gratitude, Recovery Action, and Evening Reflection.
Daily Focus and other guided experiences use choices plus optional reflection/note rather than empty blank-box-only UX.
entries.basis: Guided Today corrections and RC QA.

entries.decision: Progress is descriptive and reflective, not a recovery score.
entries.basis: RC live QA and product philosophy.

entries.decision: Recovery-date changes preserve prior history.
Persistent Help Me Right Now access remains visible and includes craving, overwhelmed, lonely, around substances, and already-used flows.
entries.basis: Approved Help Now build and RC QA.

entries.decision: Help Me Right Now and urgent safety information are never Plus-locked.
Recovery pathway is separate from belief preference.
Supported pathway options include 12-Step, SMART/skills-based, therapy/counseling, medication-supported, peer support, and faith/spiritual options.
Belief/personalization may be secular, spiritual, faith-based, mixed/exploring, with optional Christian/denomination detail including Baptist.
Ordinary Journal remains available on Free.
Journal+ / Journal Companion adds organization, collections, search, prompts, and deeper review; it does not replace the Free Journal.
Journal Companion price is $4.99/month.
entries.basis: Latest explicit pricing and live product screenshot.

entries.decision: Recovery Story may include milestones, Then & Now, goals, and guided responses the user previously approved.
Private journal material is excluded by default and must not be pulled automatically.
The user reviews included material before print/export; story editions can include 2-year, 5-year, 10-year, and custom versions.
Weekly/monthly reviews and Then & Now use guided observations plus optional reflection.
Lellee Free = $0.
Lellee Plus = $5.99/month or $59.99/year.
Lellee Premium = $14.99/month or $149/year.
Journal Companion = $4.99/month.
Lellee Coach add-on = $49.99/month in addition to/with Premium.
Additional coaching = $19.99 per 15-minute session.
Higher tiers add depth, organization, personalization, and analytical explanation—not more accurate facts.
Core recovery and safety stay free; paid tiers cannot gate Help Me Right Now, core guided recovery, core coping tools, urgent safety info, or basic resource access.
Plus at $3.99/month / $39.99/year is obsolete.
Plus price TBD / price at launch is obsolete.
A production Stripe go-live is not considered complete merely because price UI exists; production checkout/webhooks/secrets still require final verification.
entries.basis: RC launch sequence and later go-live checklist.
entries.notes: Older RC branch explicitly kept billing off; later checkout wiring exists, but production readiness remains a gate.

entries.decision: Lellee Coach remains an optional add-on above the consumer subscription, not part of the core Free experience.

Approved included service structure: first month 30-minute intake + 20-minute follow-up; thereafter two 20-minute check-ins/month, plus messaging, goals, accountability, progress review, and milestones.
Private journal access remains off/default private unless the member explicitly shares.
Ideal group size is 6–8; hard maximum 10.
Daily individual caseload target is about 6 clients/day; normal maximum about 8.
Active-user planning model is about 60 per coach, with roughly 50–70 practical and ~80 as a hard ceiling discussed.
No final W-2 versus 1099 decision is locked in the audited approvals.
entries.basis: Prior audit found no explicit user-approved classification.

entries.decision: Independent coaches can run their own businesses using the platform; Lellee members may connect only with permission.
Coach-business workspace supports 1-to-1, group, hybrid, services/packages, scheduling, groups, clients, leads/capacity, and operating metrics.
Independent-coach payment/payout marketplace behavior requires separate configuration/legal review; do not silently treat it as live.
Clients control what private Lellee information they share with a coach.
No blanket coach access to journals, safety history, unrelated program data, or private messages.
Coaching scheduling and explicitly shared goals may be available to the Coaching Agent/workflow.
Private coaching-message access defaults OFF and requires explicit per-message/per-thread sharing; revocation blocks future reads.
Coaching account/client count is hidden by default with an On/Off control; a fresh browser/session starts Off.

entries.decision: Agent Operations, Human Review, Content QA, Agent Workbench, and Workflow Copilot are support/control systems, not counted as primary agents.
Resources Agent begins search/read-only; no autonomous writes.
Housing Agent begins search-only using minimal authorized location/budget/household/accessibility/pet context; no sensitive-data sweep and no autonomous writes.
Reminder Agent may perform user-approved reminder read/create/update only; no journal/coaching-message/payment/clinical access.
Coaching Agent is limited to scheduling and explicitly shared goals; private messages remain separately consented.

Viral Content = attention/creative engine; Social = platform adaptation/publishing operations; Marketing/Growth = acquisition/conversion; Prospecting = public opportunities; Analytics = performance learning.
Virality is not guaranteed; the system optimizes for reach/engagement/signups without promising viral outcomes.
Human approval is required before publishing or outbound outreach.
Autonomous cold email, SMS, DMs, letters, and autonomous publishing are prohibited.
Agents cannot make charges/refunds/transfers/payouts or change account/security permissions.
Agents cannot make clinical diagnoses, treatment prescriptions, or emergency-disposition decisions.
Prospecting is limited to public organization/business research and reviewed outreach drafts.
Private journals, private messages, safety/crisis activity, secrets/API keys, and sensitive Recovery/health data are excluded from prospecting/marketing context.
Per-agent identity, least privilege, capability controls, audit logs, consent/revocation, independent shutdown, and admin emergency stop are approved.
User Agent Control Center exposes the user's own agent permissions/consents/activity; global kill switches remain admin-only.
Private user rows are scoped to the signed-in user with RLS; anonymous access to private user tables is denied.
Two-user isolation test is required before production: User B must not read/update/delete User A private records.
Service-role/secret keys never belong in browser code or public GitHub; browser uses publishable/anon key with RLS.
Referral requests do not include journals, private messages, safety selections, cravings, diagnoses, or full program history by default.
Organization/sponsored access does not automatically transfer ownership of a user's private account data.
Cross-program sharing remains opt-in/default off.
Signup framework is 18+ with Terms, Privacy, Consumer Health Data notice, and safety acknowledgment.
Lellee is recovery support, not an emergency service or individualized professional medical treatment.
Production legal/clinical/regulatory review remains a launch gate; build files do not certify HIPAA/42 CFR Part 2/California compliance.
Public marketing pages may remain searchable by ordinary search engines where desired, while AI training/search/agent crawlers are restricted.
robots.txt alone is not treated as a security boundary; production edge/WAF enforcement is required.
Internal Lellee agents authenticate through internal identity/capability controls; they are not identified merely by User-Agent strings.
Private journals/messages/coaching/safety/account data remain behind authentication/RLS and are never public crawler content.
Lellee is mobile-first/responsive for iPhone, Android, and desktop, with PWA/add-to-home-screen support.
Phone-width QA includes no horizontal scroll, readable text without zoom, usable touch targets, fitting overlays, and content not cut off.
Private/live account data should not be indiscriminately cached for offline use; offline support is shell-oriented.
Push is opt-in; core in-app reminders still work without push.
Hard refresh must get the latest deployment; old service workers must not resurrect stale interfaces.
A deployable package must include the complete dependency set it references; do not mix new HTML with leftover old JS/CSS.
Vercel preview/current deployment is the QA source of truth until production cutover.
Production cutover requires domain, auth redirect, legal/privacy/safety, security, billing, mobile, rollback, and analytics checks.
